The Hansard database

Source: vignettes/database.Rmd
database.Rmd

This vignette describes the database that ausparl queries: what it contains, how its tables fit together, the identifiers that link them, and the conventions behind its columns. It is a reference to keep open while you work.

Every example here runs on the small sample database bundled with the package (eight sitting days), so the numbers are small. The full database has the same tables, views and columns.

library(ausparl)
library(dplyr)
db_connect(sample = TRUE)

What is in the database

The database is one DuckDB file, hansard.duckdb, built from two sources:

  • Hansard, the official record of debates in the House of Representatives and the Senate, from 1901. Each sitting day’s transcript is parsed into its debates, subdebates and the individual contributions (actions) within them, and each speaker is matched to a member.
  • The Parliamentary Handbook of the Commonwealth of Australia, which supplies the members and their service, parties, ministries and shadow ministries, committees, presiding officers, electorates, elections, parliaments and biographical detail.

db_info() reports which build you are connected to. Quote its schema_version and built_at in your methods, so that others can reproduce your numbers.

db_info() |>
  select(schema_version, built_at, n_sittings, n_actions, n_members)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   schema_version built_at            n_sittings n_actions n_members
#>   <chr>          <dttm>                   <int>     <int>     <int>
#> 1 7.0.0          2026-11-23 13:40:39          8      1488       303

How the tables fit together

The transcript tables nest, from the sitting day down to the single contribution:

sittings        one row per sitting day of one chamber
 └ debates      one row per debate within a sitting
    └ subdebates  one row per topic within a debate (subdebates can nest)
       └ actions  one row per contribution: a speech, question, answer,
                  interjection, quote or procedural note

The Handbook tables hang off two keys: PHID, which identifies a member, and the date. A turn is linked to the member who made it through actions.PHID, and to what was true of that member on the day (their party, role, electorate) through the sitting date.

members ── PHID ──┬── parl_service          seats held, with dates
                  ├── party_service         party memberships, with dates
                  ├── ministry_records      ministerial appointments
                  ├── shadow_ministry_records
                  ├── committee_members
                  ├── presiding_officers
                  └── occupations, qualifications, schools

Identifiers

Identifier Identifies Form Example
sitting_id a sitting day of one chamber <chamber>_<date> house_2002-10-15
debate_id a debate within a sitting sitting id + _D<n> house_2002-10-15_D3
subdebate_id a subdebate within a debate debate id + _S<n> house_2002-10-15_D3_S1
action_id one action (contribution) sitting id + _R<n> house_2002-10-15_R12
PHID a member Parliamentary Handbook id ZD4 (John Howard)
parliament_id a parliament its number 40 (2002-2004)
party_id a party integer see get_parties()
electorate_id an electorate integer see get_electorates()

Look a member’s PHID up from their name with find_member():

find_member("howard")

#> 2 ZD4   HOWARD, the Hon. Joh… Male   1939-07-26  New … house    1974-05-18    2007-11-24

Actions and turns

actions is the core table: one row per contribution, with its text in content. Each action has one action_type:

get_actions(columns = "action_type", collect = FALSE) |>
  count(action_type) |>
  collect()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 2
#>   action_type                 n
#>   <chr>                   <dbl>
#> 1 unresolved_interjection    16
#> 2 speech                    566
#> 3 answer                    229
#> 4 quote                      20
#> 5 procedural                488
#> 6 question                  169
  • speech, question and answer: a member’s own contribution.
  • quote: a passage read into the record, such as a letter or petition: not the speaker’s own words.
  • procedural: a non-speech entry, such as “Mr Speaker took the chair”.
  • unresolved_interjection: an interjection whose speaker the source does not identify.

Logical flags refine the type. is_speech, is_question and is_answer mark a member’s substantive contributions, is_interjection marks interjections (including resolved ones, which have action_type = "speech"), and has_quote marks actions that contain quoted material. get_speeches() uses these flags: by default it returns speeches, questions and answers, and leaves interjections out.

A speech interrupted by interjections, or continued across pages, is several actions. Actions that belong to one uninterrupted contribution share a turn_no, and get_speech_turns() merges them into a single row per turn:

get_actions(
  sitting_id = "house_2002-10-15", is_non_speech = FALSE,
  columns = c("action_id", "turn_no", "PHID", "action_type", "is_interjection")
) |>
  arrange(turn_no) |>
  head(8)
#> # A tibble: 8 × 5
#>   action_id           turn_no PHID  action_type is_interjection
#>   <chr>                 <int> <chr> <chr>       <lgl>          
#> 1 house_2002-10-15_R2       1 ZD4   speech      FALSE          
#> 2 house_2002-10-15_R3       2 DT4   question    FALSE          
#> 3 house_2002-10-15_R4       3 ZD4   answer      FALSE          
#> 4 house_2002-10-15_R5       4 MH4   question    FALSE          
#> 5 house_2002-10-15_R6       5 7V5   answer      FALSE          
#> 6 house_2002-10-15_R7       6 4I4   question    FALSE          
#> 7 house_2002-10-15_R8       7 ZD4   answer      FALSE          
#> 8 house_2002-10-15_R9       8 AK6   question    FALSE

get_speech_turns(sitting_id = "house_2002-10-15", include_text = FALSE) |>
  select(turn_no, n_actions, PHID, party_at_time, is_quote) |>
  head()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   turn_no n_actions PHID  party_at_time              is_quote
#>     <int>     <dbl> <chr> <chr>                      <lgl>   
#> 1       1         1 ZD4   Liberal Party of Australia FALSE   
#> 2       2         1 DT4   Australian Labor Party     FALSE   
#> 3       3         1 ZD4   Liberal Party of Australia FALSE   
#> 4       4         1 MH4   Liberal Party of Australia FALSE   
#> 5       5         1 7V5   Liberal Party of Australia FALSE   
#> 6       6         1 4I4   Australian Labor Party     FALSE

get_sitting_timeline() gives a sitting in document order, with the debate and subdebate titles, and get_interjections() pairs each interjection with the turn it interrupted.

get_sitting_timeline(sitting_id = "senate_2019-11-26", include_text = FALSE) |>
  filter(action_type != "procedural") |>
  select(seq, debate_title, action_type, speaker_name) |>
  head(8)
#> # A tibble: 8 × 4
#>     seq debate_title action_type speaker_name                             
#>   <int> <chr>        <chr>       <chr>

Who spoke

Each action records the speaker as printed (name_raw, party_raw, role_raw, electorate_raw) and, where they could be matched, the member’s PHID. The resolution column says how the speaker was matched:

resolution Meaning PHID
resolved matched to one member set
sentinel the presiding officer (Speaker, President or their deputy) in the chair NA
collective a group, such as “Honourable members” or “Opposition members” NA
unknown the source records the speaker as unknown NA
unmatched a named speaker who could not be matched to a member NA
ambiguous a name that fits more than one member NA
non_member someone who is not a member, such as the Governor-General NA
NA no speaker: procedural entries, and quotes that name no reader NA 
get_actions(columns = "resolution", collect = FALSE) |>
  count(resolution) |>
  collect()
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>   resolution     n
#>   <chr>      <dbl>
#> 1 resolved     877
#> 2 collective    15
#> 3 NA           495
#> 4 unknown       17
#> 5 sentinel      84

Presiding-officer turns are left out of get_speeches() unless include_presiding = TRUE, and a member filter keeps only resolved turns.

Context on the day

A member’s party, role and electorate change over time, so the database holds them as dated periods (party_service, ministry_records, parl_service and others). Views named v_<thing>_at_time resolve them for each action on its sitting date, and the add_*() functions join those views onto any result with an action_id:

Function Adds From
add_party() the speaker’s party and its abbreviation v_party_at_time
add_role() minister, shadow minister or backbencher v_role_at_time
add_government_status() whether the speaker’s party was in government v_government_status_at_time
add_electorate() the division or state the speaker represented v_electorate_at_time
add_age() age in years v_age_at_time
add_member() name, gender, state (not dated) members
add_debate() debate and subdebate titles debates, subdebates 
get_speeches(from = "2002-10-15", to = "2002-10-15", chamber = "house",
             include_text = FALSE, limit = 5) |>
  add_party() |>
  add_government_status() |>
  select(action_id, PHID, party_abbrev_at_time, government_status_at_time)
#> Skipping party_id_at_time and party_at_time: already in `x`.
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>   action_id             PHID  party_abbrev_at_time government_status_at_time
#>   <chr>                 <chr> <chr>                <chr>                    
#> 1 house_2002-10-15_R10  SU5   NPA                  government               
#> 2 house_2002-10-15_R100 K26   ALP                  opposition               
#> 3 house_2002-10-15_R103 9V5   LIB                  government               
#> 4 house_2002-10-15_R105 9V5   LIB                  government               
#> 5 house_2002-10-15_R108 009CW ALP                  opposition

Turns without a PHID get NA in every added column.

Handbook tables and their conventions

The Handbook tables keep the Handbook’s own column names (DateStart, DisplayName, MemberOrSenator), so they read like the source. A few conventions apply across them:

  • _raw columns keep a value as it was in the source, beside a cleaned version: for example DateEnd_raw beside DateEnd, or name_raw beside PHID. Use the cleaned column for analysis and the raw one to check it.
  • handbook_flag marks rows where the Handbook itself looks wrong or inconsistent, such as overlapping terms. Flagged rows are kept, not corrected.
  • *_status and date_uncertain describe how an end date was derived, or that a date is not known exactly.
  • An end date of NA means the period is ongoing (or its end is not recorded).
  • Display views. Several getters take display = TRUE, which reads a v_<table>_display view that adds readable columns, such as the member’s DisplayName or the party colour.
  • active_during. Getters for dated tables take active_during, which keeps the periods overlapping a year, a date or an in_range().
get_party_service(PHID = "ZD4", display = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 9
#>   PHID  DateStart  DateEnd    Party      handbook_flag date_uncertain party_id DisplayName
#>   <chr> <date>     <date>     <chr>      <chr>         <lgl>             <int> <chr>      
#> 1 ZD4   1974-05-18 2007-11-24 Liberal P… NA            FALSE                 4 HOWARD, th…
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: PartyColour <chr>
get_ministry_records(PHID = "ZD4", active_during = 1996, display = TRUE) |>
  distinct(DisplayName, Role, Prep, Entity, RDateStart, RDateEnd)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   DisplayName                       Role             Prep  Entity RDateStart RDateEnd  
#>   <chr>                             <chr>            <chr> <chr>  <date>     <date>    
#> 1 HOWARD, the Hon. John Winston, AC Prime Minister   ""    ""     1996-03-11 2007-12-03
#> 2 HOWARD, the Hon. John Winston, AC Cabinet Minister ""    ""     1996-03-11 2007-12-03

Parties that merged, split or renamed are linked in party_lineage, and the spellings of party names found in the transcripts are mapped to party_id in party_alias. Neither has a getter; read them with db_tbl():

db_tbl("party_lineage") |> collect()
#> # A tibble: 9 × 5
#>   party_id related_party_id relation       from_date  note                                
#>      <int>            <int> <chr>          <date>     <chr>                               
#> 1       11               81 grouped_rename NA         Pauline Hanson's One Nation (11) an…
#> 2       27               17 grouped_rename 1906-01-01 Free Trade renamed Anti-Socialist; …
#> 3        6               65 grouped_rename NA         Nick Xenophon Team renamed Centre A…
#> 4       14               24 grouped_rename NA         Australian Labor Party (Anti-Commun…
#> 5       52                4 not_grouped    1945-02-21 Liberal Party of Australia (1944) i…
#> 6        9               57 not_grouped    2017-04-01 Family First merged into the Austra…
#> 7       50               24 not_grouped    1962-10-01 Queensland Labor Party became the D…
#> 8       49               74 not_grouped    NA         Palmer United Party vs United Austr…
#> 9       37               22 label_only     NA         Victorian Liberal and Country Party…

All tables and views 

DBI::dbGetQuery(db_con(), "
  SELECT table_name AS name,
         CASE table_type WHEN 'VIEW' THEN 'view' ELSE 'table' END AS type
  FROM information_schema.tables
  WHERE table_schema = 'main'
  ORDER BY type, name
")

Table One row per Getter
sittings sitting day get_sittings()
debates debate get_debates()
subdebates subdebate get_subdebates()
actions action (contribution) get_actions()
provenance source file get_provenance()
members member get_members()
parliaments parliament get_parliaments()
parties party get_parties()
electorates electorate get_electorates()
elections election get_elections()
parl_service period of service in a seat get_parl_service()
party_service period of party membership get_party_service()
ministries ministry and governing party get_ministries()
ministry_records ministerial appointment get_ministry_records()
shadow_ministry_records shadow ministerial appointment get_shadow_ministry_records()
committee_members committee membership get_committee_members()
presiding_officers presiding office held get_presiding_officers()
occupations, qualifications, schools member and item get_occupations(), get_qualifications(), get_schools()
party_alias, party_lineage party name spelling; party relation db_tbl()
schema_version the build (one row) db_info()
parse_errors transcript that could not be parsed db_tbl()

The columns of any table or view are listed by colnames(db_tbl("<name>")), and every getter’s help page lists its columns as filter arguments.

Provenance

Every sitting can be traced to the transcript file it was parsed from, with the file’s SHA-256 checksum and the parser generation that read it. result_provenance() does this for any result:

get_speeches(from = "1902-10-10", to = "1902-10-10", include_text = FALSE, limit = 3) |>
  result_provenance()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   path    sha256 schema_generation parsed_at           input_row_count output_action_count
#>   <chr>   <chr>  <chr>             <dttm>                        <int>               <int>
#> 1 ../dat… 5261c… v2.1              2026-11-23 10:31:39             105                 102
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: sitting_id <chr>, source <chr>
db_disconnect()
